assessor: RTS governed build assessment — False-Green Test Adequacy Gate v1
rationale: K1 now has a strong human-escalation contract, but its 76-item green result is only as trustworthy as the tests that can detect violations of that contract. K2 adds an independent repository-local adequacy layer: known-bad injection, valid critical mutants, held-out fixtures, metamorphic checks, and harness controls. The layer does not change K1 runtime logic and is designed to fail closed when a behavioral fault survives or when the mutation harness cannot distinguish semantic failures from invalid mutants.

assets.notes: K2 mutates a temporary copy or structured behavior surface only; production K1 is not edited in-place.
Targeted K1 behavioral tests are the mutation kill oracle.

gaps: No layer verifies that K1 tests kill deliberate semantic faults.
No layer distinguishes a meaningful mutation kill from syntax/import failure.
No positive control proves the mutation harness does not kill equivalent behavior.
No independent held-out lane guards against tuning to the original 76-item surface.
No metamorphic lane verifies decision stability under meaning-preserving representation changes.

risks: Mutation operators may become stale when K1 source changes.
A mutation may be invalid rather than behaviorally wrong and create a false kill.
Known-bad fixtures may accidentally duplicate K1 training/DA fixtures.
Metamorphic transformations may alter semantics unintentionally.
Mutation kill percentage can become a vanity metric if lane-specific failures are hidden.
